target_customer: Originally Mexican knowledge workers paid in USD by US employers; later US-Mexico businesses, especially freight and logistics
problem: Remote workers in Mexico lose money to hidden FX and transfer fees across several accounts. Coba offered a dual currency account to earn in USD and spend in pesos.
business_model: Fintech account and cards with FX and transfer fees; later cross-border payments infrastructure for businesses

founders.name: Carlos Alberto Medellin Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; CEO title from a search summary.

founders.name: Abraham Kuri Vargas
education: B.S. in Computer Science and Technology (school not stated)
founders.background_notes: Author of APIs on Rails per YC page.

founders.name: Eduardo Lopez De Leon
founders.background_notes: Developer by training with 10+ years building technology companies per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs banking partners on both sides of the border, card issuing and compliance, which is mostly integration and regulatory work rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on partner banks and licenses; Wise, Revolut and Nubank can offer similar multi-currency products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Nubank entered Mexico in 2022 and Revolut later obtained a Mexican banking licence in 2025 per search results; Coba moved toward B2B freight payments.

market_need_then: Mexican professionals paid by US firms face FX spreads and multi-hop transfers; the company cites about $1,000 per year lost to hidden fees.

identity.voice_and_tone: Not assessed; coba.ai site fetch was rate limited

brand_strength.rationale: Short invented name but little evidence of brand level press or community; sources focus on funding and product.

pivots.from: Consumer dual currency accounts for Mexican remote workers
pivots.to: Cross-border financial infrastructure for US-Mexico businesses with a freight and logistics focus
pivots.why: Not stated by a primary source; profiles from 2025 describe the shift.

outcome_analysis: Coba raised a $2.2M seed in February 2024 after YC Summer 2023 and remains active. Later profiles describe a move from a consumer account to B2B cross-border payments for freight, suggesting the consumer wedge was narrow while neobanks expanded in Mexico. No later round was found, so it is early and still unproven.
notes: Seed dates vary by source (30 January, 8 February, 15 February 2024); Contxto published 15 February 2024. Contxto names Joseph Saliba and Eduardo Lopez as co-founders and describes Medellin and Kuri as colleagues, while YC lists Medellin, Kuri and Lopez; Saliba is not listed above because the YC page does not name him. Coba.ai fetch was rate limited. No dated competitor sources near mid 2023 were found (results were 2025 to 2026), so the list is empty. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
